description: An empty pre-commit AND post-commit stat passes both halves of the anti-clobber check on a commit that carries nothing

An **empty stat on BOTH sides** of a commit is the signal that someone published
your work first — not that you had nothing to commit.

I wrote a 60-line commit message withdrawing five of my own published claims
(source corrections I had just made and verified). Pre-commit `diff --cached

the publisher. A run **terminating** also sweeps the shared tree, so the exposure
window is not only "between your read-tree and your commit" — a run you are not
part of, exiting, is enough. See [[private-index-does-not-protect-the-message]].

**How to apply:** when the pre-commit stat is empty, stop and ask *why* before
concluding there was nothing to do — `git log -S "<a string you just wrote>"` names
the commit that took it. And do not read "both checks passed" as "my commit is
correct"; on an empty commit both checks are vacuous. The two polarities to grep
for in the shared index are your own paths staged `D` (deletion) **and** staged `M`
against a stale blob (silent revert) — I had one of each, from one session, on a
two-path payload; hashing `HEAD:<path>` against disk passed on both and cannot
